page: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v5 is a memory-optimized instance engineered for large-scale enterprise workloads requiring substantial memory capacity and high multi-threaded CPU throughput. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the virtual machine provides 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It is driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processor running at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, complemented by 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Architectural capabilities include hardware acceleration flags for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Hardware resource sizing includes 672.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 7.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a bundled 3,865 GB local SSD storage volume. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show distinct execution characteristics. While single-thread performance registers in the middle tier—yielding 1,899.99 in stress-ng single-core and 1,707.0 in Geekbench single-core—parallel performance scales into the top tier. Multi-core evaluations show a stress-ng score of 93,253.55, a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,696.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 76,733.99. Strong hardware cryptography capabilities emerge in the PassMark encryption test, which reached 87,470.54, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems.

Data-intensive operations leverage high memory bandwidth, achieving 330.43 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 135.06 GB/sec for uncached writes. The server delivered 91.6 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 30,980.2 in PassMark database benchmarks. With 3,865 GB of local SSD and no bundled GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, the instance trades per-thread latency for aggregate core and memory density, making it best fitted for large in-memory databases, distributed caching, massive compilation pipelines, and enterprise relational database deployments.
description: Microsoft Azure E96ds_v5 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. Equipped with 672.0 GB of memory and 3,865 GB of local SSD storage, it delivers an expansive resource profile without bundled GPU accelerators. Multi-threaded benchmark testing demonstrates strong performance, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,696.0 and top-tier PassMark encryption performance of 87,470.54. Single-core performance falls in the average tier, prioritizing scale-out core count and memory bandwidth over individual thread speeds. The large RAM capacity, rapid local disk, and solid multi-core throughput make the instance well fitted for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale caching engines, data analytics, and relational database systems.
